meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why was Owen's grade changed without anyone calling me first?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Go on.

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing down 11:52 PM and 11:58 PM. Students draft elsewhere and paste it in, so what does that prove?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Okay. Whatever happens, this stays off his record and it stays quiet. What else do you have besides this?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
I'm searching the scene now. A wrong quote is a student misremembering, or pulling it from the wrong act. Is that all this is?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Okay. I'll want both of those in writing, with the dates. What exactly are you proposing?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay; that's called revising. And you still haven't told me what you're proposing.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Fine. I'll agree to the rewrite to put this behind him, not because he did anything. Private, nothing on his record, in writing tonight.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
I'll confirm it with Owen tonight. Put the time and who supervises in the same email as the rest.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

You agreed to a private, supervised rewrite of Owen's essay under procedure 4.4, after school on Thursday the twelfth, with its mark replacing the zero. I still require written confirmation that nothing goes on his record, along with the time and who supervises. I expect it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: Her last position, accepting a private supervised rewrite to put this behind him, and she still wants the written promise that nothing goes on his record, plus the time and the supervisor; that is the fair outcome under 4.4, and her clock did not run out first.
What moved her: You showed the version history with its times and answered her paste-it-in defence by offering to look at any earlier draft, which gave her something she could check and moved her off her opening demand.
What cost ground: Nothing; you owned the zero in one sentence, led with a document instead of the checker score, and never accused Owen.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the writing late at night in October, at 11:52 PM and 11:58 PM, which sits close to that night, though it proves nothing about the essay and is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she pushed back that students revise their arguments between outline and essay, answer that point before moving on to the offer, so it does not stay open for her email.
